title: MTH 101 — 1st Semester CBT Mock Exam: Algebra, Sets & Binomial Series
description: [1st Semester] Timed CBT practice covering set theory, quadratic roots, binomial theorem, and complex numbers.

questions.question_text: If α and β are the roots of the quadratic equation 2x² - 8x + 5 = 0, what is the value of α + β?
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c = 0, sum of roots α + β = -b/a = -(-8)/2 = 4.

questions.question_text: In a class of 50 students, 30 offer MTH 101 and 25 offer PHY 101. If every student offers at least one of the two courses, how many offer both?
What is the coefficient of x³ in the binomial expansion of (1 + 2x)⁴?
questions.explanation: The x³ term is C(4, 3)(1)¹(2x)³ = 4 × 8x³ = 32x³.

questions.question_text: Evaluate i²⁵ where i = √(-1).
questions.explanation: Since i⁴ = 1, i²⁵ = (i⁴)⁶ · i¹ = 1 · i = i.

questions.question_text: For what value of k does the quadratic equation x² + 6x + k = 0 have equal real roots?
questions.explanation: Equal roots occur when Δ = b² - 4ac = 0 => 6² - 4(1)(k) = 0 => 36 = 4k => k = 9.

course_name: General Physics I: Mechanics, Thermal Physics & Properties of Matter
title: PHY 101 — 1st Semester CBT Mock Exam: Mechanics & Kinematics
description: [1st Semester] Timed CBT practice covering dimensional analysis, projectile motion, Newton's laws, and energy conservation.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched with an initial speed of 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal (take g = 10 m/s²). What is its time of flight?
Which of the following represents the correct dimensional formula for Young's Modulus of Elasticity?
questions.explanation: Young's Modulus = Stress / Strain. Since strain is dimensionless, it has the dimensions of pressure/stress: Force / Area = (M L T⁻²) / L² = M L⁻¹ T⁻².

questions.question_text: A 4 kg body moving at 6 m/s collides with a stationary 2 kg body and they stick together. What is their common velocity after collision?
questions.explanation: By conservation of linear momentum: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = (m₁ + m₂)v => 4(6) + 0 = (4 + 2)v => v = 24 / 6 = 4 m/s.

questions.question_text: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg mass moving with a linear momentum of 10 kg·m/s?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy K = p² / (2m) = 10² / (2 × 2) = 100 / 4 = 25 J.

course_name: Elementary Mathematics II: Differential & Integral Calculus
title: MTH 102 — 2nd Semester CBT Mock Exam: Differential & Integral Calculus
description: [2nd Semester] Timed CBT exam covering limits, L'Hôpital's rule, derivatives, and definite integration.

questions.question_text: Evaluate lim_{x -> 0} (sin 5x) / x.
questions.explanation: Using lim_{u -> 0} (sin u)/u = 1, lim_{x -> 0} 5 · (sin 5x)/(5x) = 5 × 1 = 5.

questions.question_text: Find the derivative dy/dx of y = x³ - 4x² + 7x - 2 at x = 2.
Evaluate the definite integral ∫₀² (3x² + 2x) dx.
questions.explanation: Antiderivative is [x³ + x²]₀² = (2³ + 2²) - 0 = 8 + 4 = 12.

questions.question_text: What is the derivative of f(x) = ln(x² + 1)?
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, d/dx [ln(u)] = u'/u = 2x / (x² + 1).

course_name: General Physics II: Electricity, Magnetism & Modern Physics
title: PHY 102 — 2nd Semester CBT Mock Exam: Electrostatics & DC Circuits
description: [2nd Semester] Timed CBT practice covering Coulomb's law, capacitance, Ohm's law, and Kirchhoff's circuit rules.

questions.question_text: Two capacitors of capacitance 6 μF and 3 μF are connected in series. What is their equivalent capacitance?
questions.explanation: For series capacitors: C_eq = (C₁ × C₂) / (C₁ + C₂) = (6 × 3) / (6 + 3) = 18 / 9 = 2 μF.

questions.question_text: Calculate the energy stored in a 10 μF capacitor charged to a potential difference of 100 V.
A 12 V battery of negligible internal resistance is connected across two parallel resistors of 4 Ω and 12 Ω. What is the total current drawn from the battery?
questions.explanation: Equivalent parallel resistance R_eq = (4 × 12)/(4 + 12) = 48/16 = 3 Ω. Total current I = V / R_eq = 12 V / 3 Ω = 4 A.

questions.question_text: According to Gauss's Law, the net electric flux through any closed surface enclosing a total charge Q is equal to:
questions.explanation: Gauss's law states that the total electric flux Φ_E through any closed surface is Q_enclosed / ε₀.

course_name: General Chemistry II: Organic & Analytical Chemistry
title: CHE 102 — 2nd Semester CBT Mock Exam: Equilibrium, Acids/Bases & Organic Chemistry
description: [2nd Semester] Timed CBT exam covering chemical equilibrium, pH calculations, hybridization, and functional groups.

questions.question_text: What is the hybridization of the carbon atoms in ethyne (C₂H₂)?
questions.explanation: Each carbon atom in ethyne (HC≡CH) forms a triple bond and is sp-hybridized with a linear bond angle of 180°.

questions.question_text: What is the pH of a 0.01 M aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid (HCl)?
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong monoprotic acid, so [H⁺] = 0.01 M = 10⁻² M. pH = -log₁₀(10⁻²) = 2.

questions.question_text: Which functional group characterizes alkanoic (carboxylic) acids?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic (alkanoic) acids contain the carboxyl functional group -COOH.

questions.question_text: According to Le Chatelier's Principle, increasing the pressure on the exothermic equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) shifts the equilibrium toward:
questions.explanation: There are 4 moles of gas on the left and 2 moles of gas on the right. Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium toward fewer gas moles (right).
